hints: Notice the incident nucleus moves horizontally and the target is stationary, so the total momentum perpendicular to that line is initially zero.
For the two nuclei after collision, resolve each momentum into forward and transverse components and require the transverse components to add to zero.
Check which diagram has both outgoing paths on the same side of the incident line so their transverse momenta add rather than cancel.
walkthrough: The incident momentum is along the horizontal line and the stationary nucleus has zero momentum, so total initial momentum has no component perpendicular to that line.
In a vacuum with no other particles, total vector momentum $p$ must be conserved, so the vector sum of the two final momenta must also have zero perpendicular component.
That means the two outgoing nuclei must go to opposite sides of the incident line, so one upward transverse momentum can cancel the other downward transverse momentum.
In diagrams A, B and D one path is above and one is below the incident line, so cancellation is possible with suitable speeds and angles.
In the remaining diagram both outgoing paths lie below the incident line, giving a net downward momentum with nothing to balance it. This is option C.

options.A: One nucleus moves up and the other moves down, so their transverse momenta can cancel to zero.
options.B: One nucleus moves up and the other moves almost forward, so the vector sum can still equal the initial forward momentum.
options.C: Both nuclei move to the same side of the initial path, so there is a net transverse momentum that cannot match the zero initial transverse momentum.
options.D: One nucleus moves up and the other moves down, so the total momentum perpendicular to the incident direction can be zero.
